Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: Mali’s online tax payment platform aims to secure state revenue by direct transfer of funds into the Treasury’s single account, indicating active digital revenue collection (at least for large/mid-sized companies).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed, code unchanged. Comments: The Central Bank of West African States (BCEAO) directly operates/manages the WAEMU Automated Interbank Clearing System (SICA-UEMOA) and the WAEMU Automated Transfer and Settlement System (STAR-UEMOA) under Regulation No. 15/2002/CM/WAMU (Article 3), including operational and technical management and producing regular reports.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: Mali (as a WAEMU member) relies on BCEAO-managed interbank payment systems rather than a Mali-only inclusive instant retail payment system; AfricaNenda’s SIIPS 2023 report does not list Mali as having a live domestic instant payment system, and notes WAEMU’s regional instant payment system (IPS) was in pilot/development (16 participants; expected 2023) including Mali as one of the eight member countries.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed from 'Under development' (3) to 'Partially deployed' (4). BCEAO's regional instant payment platform PI-SPI officially launched 30 September 2025 and has been operating live, 24/7, across all eight WAEMU states since then. As of April 2026, BCEAO's own data show 11 authorised participating institutions in Mali (banks, e-money issuers, microfinance), but onboarding of all banks/e-money issuers is not required until 30 September 2026 and of microfinance institutions until 30 June 2027, so the system is live in Mali but deployment is not yet complete nationwide (code 4, not 5).

Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: World Bank reports that only 38% of Malian adults received a digital payment in 2021, implying active digital payment users are <50% of adults.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed from '20-49%' (2) to '50-69%' (3). The Global Findex 2025 microdata (survey fielded 2024/25) show 59.8% of Malian adults made or received a digital payment, up from 38% recorded in the 2021 Global Findex used for the original score; this is a genuine, methodologically comparable improvement that moves Mali into the 50-69% band.
